annotation.title_clean: Reducing Interference in Human–Robot Collaboration: A Distance-Based Policy for Disassembly Collaborative Task
annotation.title_en: Reducing Interference in Human–Robot Collaboration: A Distance-Based Policy for Disassembly Collaborative Task
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kurniawan, W.C.; Yeoh, W.L.; Fukuda, O.
annotation.venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications (IJACSA)
annotation.summary_en: Experimental study of human-robot collaborative e-waste disassembly using a DOBOT MG400 and YOLOv8 vision. It compares a distance-based safety algorithm with an unconstrained one across separate and shared target tasks, measuring completion time, warning distance, heatmaps and NASA-TLX workload. The safety policy reduces movement interference.
key_provisions_or_claims: Safety algorithm directs robot to the screw farthest from the human hand.
Four danger zones (danger, caution, warning, safe) derived from normalized human-robot distance.
Safety algorithm significantly reduced spatial distribution of human movement versus unconstrained trials.
Separate-target tasks improved human awareness of warning distances compared with shared-target tasks.
Aligning task assignment with safety algorithms reduces need for human intervention.
